title: dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics (KV-affinity, scheduling)
author: Ethan Walker
body: Motivation: reduce wasted computation and improve throughput/latency on mixed-length workloads by grouping requests by sequence-length buckets, minimizing padding, and prioritizing KV-cache affinity in the continuous batching scheduler. This PR iterates on prior seqlen bucketing work (see ENG-1842, prior PRs) and adds: 1) a bucket assignment heuristic that balances bucket fullness vs. padding overhead, 2) padding-minimization scoring to prefer batches that reduce average padded tokens, 3) KV-cache affinity for in-flight sessions to keep hot KV caches on the same worker where possible, and 4) scheduler changes to prefer low-padding batches under tight latency SLOs. Changes are designed to be opt-in via runtime config flags and have unit/integration tests and end-to-end perf benches. Implementation notes: the new BucketingScheduler computes an expected padded-token cost for candidate groupings and uses a weighted objective combining batch utilization, expected padding waste, and KV-affinity score. To avoid tail latency regressions, there is an aggressive timeout-based flush policy and a fast path for single-request low-latency mode. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged unless the new "seqlen_bucketing_v2" feature flag is enabled. Checklist: (x) design doc linked (ENG-1842) (x) experiments and benchmarks included (x) unit tests and integration tests (x) guarded behind feature flag (x) rollout plan in description ( ) docs update (small addendum required) Benchmarks summary: running mixed-length synthetic workload (mix = {short:45%, mid:35%, long:20%}) on p4d-like instance: - throughput +18% at target latency SLOs (p95 latency unchanged or improved) - p95 latency improved by ~12% on mid-heavy workloads due to reduced padding overhead - average padded tokens per batch reduced by 22% - tail-case (all-long) unchanged vs baseline due to conservative flush policy These results were measured with the feature flag enabled and KV-affinity heuristics on. Related: ENG-1842 (bucketing design), ENG-1901 (continuous-batching rewrite), SUP-482 (customer incident that motivated KV-affinity). Merge strategy: squash merge after perf signoff from @Lina Chen and @Marco Alvarez. Rolling deploy notes: enable seqlen_bucketing_v2 in staging, verify p95 and token-cost delta, then canary 5% on a low-risk region before global rollout.

Add padding-cost estimator and scoring function
Integrate KV-affinity scoring into scheduler decision path
Add unit tests for bucket assignment and timeout flush policy
Add integration bench harness and perf measurement scripts
Fix KV-cache eviction bug when affinity score ties
Add feature flag gating and config schema
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (reran once after flaky timeout fix)
review_comments: Lina Chen: Can we quantify the cost of KV-affinity on cold starts? Author: KV-affinity is scored but not enforced; cold-start penalty measured <2% in our benchmarks - added a note in bench README.
Marco Alvarez: The flush timeout looks aggressive for some enterprise SLOs. Author: made it configurable per deployment and added conservative default that matches current behavior.
Priya Raman: Please add an integration test for mixed-workload with sessions to cover KV cache hotness. Author: Added tests/integration/test_seqlen_bench.py and updated bench harness.
Carlos Gutierrez: minor nit on config naming. Author: renamed flag to seqlen_bucketing_v2 and updated config schema.
Lina Chen: Perf numbers look good; approve after doc addendum. Lina Chen: APPROVED
perf_results: throughput: +18% on mixed workload (p4d-like) at same latency SLOs
kv_cache_changes: Add cache_affinity scoring module to bias scheduling toward nodes with hot KV cache
Track per-session last-worker and increment affinity score on reuse
Eviction fix: do not evict if affinity score above threshold and node has spare memory
scheduling_changes: Add BucketingScheduler that groups by sequence-length ranges and computes padding cost
Integrate padding_cost estimator into scheduling objective
Add timeout-based flush policy and low-latency fast path
merge_commit: squash: dynamic batching seqlen bucketing + KV-affinity improvements (E. Walker)
release_notes: Introduce optional sequence-length bucketing scheduler (seqlen_bucketing_v2) that reduces padding waste for mixed-length traffic. Feature off by default; can be enabled via feature flag. Improves throughput and reduces cost for many workloads. Add rollout guidance in docs/ops/rollout-notes.md.
